patches.find: Two realistic approaches both converge on Frosty Pass, the real staging ground for the climb. Via Monument 78 (Manning Provincial Park, BC): from the Monument 78/83 trailhead on BC Highway 3 (~3,750 ft), follow the Pacific Crest Trail south about 8 miles to the Monument 78 US/Canada border crossing, then continue roughly 4 more miles on the PCT to Castle Pass — about 12 miles and ~2,450 ft of gain for a long first day. Water and camping right at Castle Pass are poor; the nearest reliable water is about a mile down in Route Creek Basin. From Castle Pass, pick up the Boundary Trail and climb about 4 more miles and ~2,200 ft to Frosty Pass, then drop a short distance into Upper Frosty Basin, a roomy trailside camp at roughly 6,100 ft with water nearby — the standard base camp for Blizzard Peak and neighboring Mt. Winthrop. Via Harts Pass (WA side): from the Harts Pass trailhead (~6,200 ft, the highest drivable pass in Washington), follow the PCT north over Windy Pass, Tamarack/Foggy/Jim Pass and down to Holman Pass (~5,100 ft, mile ~13.5 from Harts Pass), then climb back up and over Rock Pass and Woody Pass to the Devils Stairway/Hopkins Pass area (mile ~22-24) before reaching Castle Pass around mile 25-26 — a longer, more physically punishing option with several thousand feet of cumulative up-and-down before you even turn toward Frosty Pass on the Boundary Trail, but it avoids the border-crossing logistics of the Monument 78 option.
